newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ATHLETICS-INJURY TO BAR ENQUIST FROM WORLD INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-INJURY TO BAR ENQUIST FROM WORLD INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Olympic champion hurdler Ludmila Enquist said on Friday that injury would bar her from competing in the world indoor athletics championships in Paris next month.
Enquist said she had never planned to run the 60 metres hurdles in Paris but had considered competing in the 200 metres.
But a hamstring injury had kept her from training in the past week and she planned to spend another week resting.
Enquist was forced to pull out of an international indoor athletics meeting in Stockholm on Thursday due to injury.
"It's nothing major," said Enquist, 32. "I don't think there is any sprinter who has not had this.
"I have been doing next to nothing -- jogging, stretching and swimming. I have no pain when I am walking but I haven't yet tried to run."
Russia-born Enquist, who won gold for Sweden at the Atlanta Olympics, set a world best for the 100 metres indoor hurdles earlier this month.
